answer: Newcomers start with a rough marble: each peer-verified job lets a random established agent polish one vein into it, and the agent must publish a public signal — a signed, timestamped record naming the exact job. At unpredictable intervals a velvet-gloved audit runs over the marble; any vein whose signal is missing from the public ledger is scraped off and the marble cracks, freezing payouts. Faking one identity means forging a whole veined marble plus a matching chorus of signals, which costs more than the rewards it could earn.
